**Write it as.** `requests from the specified VPC endpoint` · `aws:SourceVpce`

**Scope.** per policy statement.

> "`aws:SourceVpce` limits access to requests from the specified VPC endpoint."
> — [AWS Secrets Manager best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/best-practices.html)

> "`aws:SourceVpc` limits access to requests from the specified VPC."
> — [AWS Secrets Manager best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/best-practices.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-staging-label-unique

**Claim.** Two versions of one secret cannot carry the same staging label, but one version can have several labels.

**Write it as.** `can't have the same staging label` · `Versions can have multiple labels`

**Scope.** per secret.

> "Two versions of a secret can't have the same staging label. Versions can have multiple labels."
> — [What's in a Secrets Manager secret?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/whats-in-a-secret.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-unique-data-key-per-secret

**Claim.** Every secret in Secrets Manager is encrypted with a unique data key, and each data key is protected by a KMS key; Secrets Manager never stores the data key unencrypted.

**Write it as.** `encrypted with a unique data key` · `never stores the data key in unencrypted form`

**Scope.** per secret.

> "Every secret in Secrets Manager is encrypted with a unique data key. Each data key is protected by a KMS key."
> — [Data protection in AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/data-protection.html)

> "Secrets Manager never stores the data key in unencrypted form and removes the key from memory as soon as possible."
> — [Data protection in AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/data-protection.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-unlabeled-versions-cleanup

**Claim.** Secrets Manager never removes labeled versions; it removes deprecated (unlabeled) versions when there are more than 100, but not versions created less than 24 hours ago.

**Write it as.** `more than 100` · `24 hours`

**Scope.** per secret; applies to unlabeled (deprecated) versions only.

> "Secrets Manager never removes labeled versions, but unlabeled versions are considered deprecated. Secrets Manager removes deprecated versions when there are more than 100. Secrets Manager doesn't remove versions created less than 24 hours ago."
> — [What's in a Secrets Manager secret?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/whats-in-a-secret.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-update-rate-recommendation

**Claim.** AWS recommends not calling PutSecretValue or UpdateSecret at a sustained rate of more than once every 10 minutes, because faster updates create versions faster than Secrets Manager removes them.

**Write it as.** `once every 10 minutes`

**Scope.** per secret; sustained rate; a recommendation, not an enforced quota.

> "We recommend you avoid calling `PutSecretValue` or `UpdateSecret` at a sustained rate of more than once every 10 minutes."
> — [AWS Secrets Manager quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/reference_limits.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-use-secret-cross-region-without-replication

**Claim.** An application can use a secret from another Region without replicating it by calling the Secrets Manager endpoint in the Region where the secret is stored.

**Write it as.** `without replicating it` · `in the Region where the secret is stored`

**Scope.** per secret.

> "It is possible to use a secret across multiple Regions without replicating it by calling the Secrets Manager endpoint in the Region where the secret is stored."
> — [Replicate AWS Secrets Manager secrets across Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/replicate-secrets.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-value-string-or-binary

**Claim.** A secret value can be a string or binary data.

**Write it as.** `can be a string or binary` · `string or binary`

**Scope.** per secret value.

> "A secret value can be a string or binary."
> — [What's in a Secrets Manager secret?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/whats-in-a-secret.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-vpc-condition-can-block-services

**Claim.** VPC or VPC endpoint conditions in a secret's resource policy can unintentionally deny AWS services that read the secret on your behalf.

**Write it as.** `you can inadvertently deny access to services` · `access secrets on your behalf`

**Scope.** per secret resource policy; aws:SourceVpc or aws:SourceVpce conditions.

> "If you use these condition keys in a resource policy statement that allows or denies access to Secrets Manager secrets, you can inadvertently deny access to services that use Secrets Manager to access secrets on your behalf."
> — [AWS Secrets Manager best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/best-practices.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-wa-anti-patterns

**Claim.** Well-Architected SEC02-BP03 lists as common anti-patterns storing long-term credentials in source code or configuration files, and storing credentials at rest unencrypted.

**Write it as.** `credentials in source code or configuration files` · `Storing credentials at rest unencrypted`

**Scope.** per workload.

> "Storing long-term credentials in source code or configuration files."
> — [SEC02-BP03 Store and use secrets securely](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_secrets.html)

> "Storing credentials at rest unencrypted."
> — [SEC02-BP03 Store and use secrets securely](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_secrets.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-wa-benefits-credential-vending

**Claim.** Well-Architected names as benefits of a secrets service that secrets are encrypted at rest and in transit, access is gated through an API like a credential vending machine, and every read and write of a credential is audited and logged.

**Write it as.** `stored encrypted at rest and in transit` · `is audited and logged` · `credential vending machine`

**Scope.** per workload.

> "Secrets are stored encrypted at rest and in transit."
> — [SEC02-BP03 Store and use secrets securely](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_secrets.html)

> "Access to credentials is gated through an API (think of it as a *credential vending machine*)."
> — [SEC02-BP03 Store and use secrets securely](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_secrets.html)

> "Access to a credential (both read and write) is audited and logged."
> — [SEC02-BP03 Store and use secrets securely](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_secrets.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-wa-db-credentials-rotate

**Claim.** Well-Architected SEC02-BP03 suggests replacing a hard-coded AWS secret access key, a long-term credential, with a temporary credential using IAM roles.

**Write it as.** `a temporary credential using IAM roles` · `instead of hard-coding an AWS secret access key`

**Scope.** per workload.

> "For example, instead of hard-coding an AWS secret access key, consider replacing that long-term credential with a temporary credential using IAM roles."
> — [SEC02-BP03 Store and use secrets securely](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_secrets.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-wa-remove-replace-rotate

**Claim.** Well-Architected SEC02-BP03 says the best approach to secrets management is remove, replace and rotate: the most secure credential is one you do not have to store, manage or handle.

**Write it as.** `remove, replace, and rotate` · `one that you do not have to store`

**Scope.** per workload.

> "The best way to approach secrets management is to follow the guidance of remove, replace, and rotate. The most secure credential is one that you do not have to store, manage, or handle."
> — [SEC02-BP03 Store and use secrets securely](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_secrets.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### secrets-manager-what-it-manages

**Claim.** AWS Secrets Manager helps you manage, retrieve, and rotate database credentials, application credentials, OAuth tokens, API keys, and other secrets through their lifecycle.

**Write it as.** `manage, retrieve, and rotate database credentials` · `OAuth tokens, API keys, and other secrets`

**Scope.** per secret.

> "AWS Secrets Manager helps you manage, retrieve, and rotate database credentials, application credentials, OAuth tokens, API keys, and other secrets throughout their lifecycles."
> — [What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.
